The rooms are reasonably sized and come with basic furniture such as a bed, cupboard, study table, and chair. While the facilities are simple, they are sufficient for comfortable living. Cleanliness is maintained fairly well, with regular housekeeping services provided. However, there is still some room for improvement in maintaining common areas like the kitchen and corridors.

The food quality is average but manageable. Meals are served on time, and the menu changes regularly, which prevents it from becoming too repetitive. That said, the taste may not suit everyone, and sometimes the spice levels vary. Wi-Fi connectivity is stable most of the time, making it suitable for online work and study.

The PG owner and staff are cooperative and responsive to complaints or maintenance requests. Security arrangements such as CCTV cameras and restricted entry add an extra layer of safety.

Overall, this PG offers good value for money. It may not provide luxury facilities, but it covers all the basic needs for a comfortable and convenient stay. [{"Name":"Anshika Goyal","ProfilePicture":"https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/a/ACg8ocJGKsgR4TkYERacjvW6caIclFtfKyldG_0eG4bnnS3qCs1tnQ=s120-c-rp-mo-br100","Rating":1,"Description":"Extremely disappointed with Clanbridge’s management and post-checkout experience.

My stay itself was mostly pleasant , rooms were good and food was fine. However, maintenance was extremely slow. On the very day I moved in, the toilet jet in my room was found broken and it took them 3 days to send someone to get it fixed. Generally, maintenance issues took several days and required repeated follow-ups, otherwise it won't even be done. Wardens frequently did not pick up calls, which made even basic issues unnecessarily frustrating.

The worst experience started after I checked out on 31 May 2026. My ₹20,000 security deposit was returned after around 45 days despite the agreement stating a 30-day period, with ₹2,500 deducted for alleged wall damage/repainting (I had tape residue from a few posters over a my desk wall).

I am completely willing to pay for genuine damage caused by me. However, I was told that the entire room had been repainted to make the paint even and I have to pay for it. I have geotagged photographs dated 30 July 2026 showing that the room/walls had still not been repainted. Also, the back wall already had tape marks/dirt when I moved in and wasn't repainted then.

After weeks of emails and calls, I finally received my signed agreement and could not find the claimed minimum ₹2,500 wall-paint deduction. I was then provided a handwritten/informal painter’s bill dated 06/06/2026 for ₹2,880 (48 sq. ft. × ₹60), with no invoice number, GSTIN or clear business details, while my geotagged photographs from 30 July show the condition of the walls weeks after the claimed work.

The sales team's handling has been extremely frustrating, stressful and disappointing. Emails went unanswered, calls required constant follow-ups, and I had to repeatedly chase them simply to get my own agreement and justification for my money.

Start with the basics. Clean, well ventilated rooms matter more than fancy interiors. Proper beds, sturdy wardrobes, study tables, and enough storage space make daily life easier. Good lighting and windows for fresh air are underrated features that improve comfort and health over time.
Reliable food service is another huge factor. Many PGs provide home style meals with breakfast and dinner included. Consistent quality, hygienic kitchens, and a rotating menu help residents avoid the daily stress of finding food after work.
High speed WiFi has quietly become one of the most essential amenities. Working professionals often need stable internet for office work, meetings, or simply relaxing with entertainment after a long day.
Security is critical. A good PG usually has CCTV cameras, secure entry systems, and sometimes even a caretaker or guard. This creates a safe environment, especially for residents who return late from work.
Housekeeping services add significant value. Regular cleaning of rooms, bathrooms, and common areas keeps the place hygienic and reduces the burden on residents who already have busy schedules.
Power backup is another practical feature. In cities where electricity cuts happen occasionally, a generator or inverter ensures that lights, fans, and WiFi keep running.
Laundry facilities are also important. Many PGs provide washing machines or laundry services, saving residents time and effort.
Common areas can improve the overall living experience. Spaces like a shared lounge, dining area, or small recreation space allow residents to relax and interact with others living there.
Location plays a massive role as well. A PG close to offices, metro stations, markets, and food outlets makes commuting easier and daily errands faster.
Parking availability is useful for residents who own bikes or cars. Even simple bike parking can make a big difference.
Finally, a supportive and responsive management team ties everything together. When the owner or caretaker quickly resolves issues like maintenance, water supply, or internet problems, the PG becomes a place people genuinely enjoy living in.
A good PG is not just about a room. The owners and the PG manager were one of the best parts of my stay. They were polite, respectful, and never interfered unnecessarily. Whenever I had to change rooms (which happened twice during my stay), the process was handled without any issues. They had also provided a water cooler, which was helpful during summers.

The locality has a village-like feel and isn't very modern, but the low rent makes it a fair trade-off.

The main area that needs improvement is the kitchen and food management. The food quality and menu were often disappointing, and breakfast was especially difficult. Everyone had to wait for fresh rotis every morning because the cook struggled to serve everyone on time, which caused many working professionals to get late for their offices. Another issue was the utensil washing sink on the rooftop, which was frequently clogged and unhygienic. Overflowing dirty water often spilled onto people's clothes and feet, making it unpleasant to use.

The ground floor was also used to park and charge e-rickshaws, which sometimes made the entrance feel congested.

Overall, I would highly rate the owners and the management for their behaviour and the value for money.
